subject: Throughput & Latency Compensation — Proposal and Next Steps
messages:
From: Kevin Hayes <kevin.hayes@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-04-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Major throughput & latency surge — urgent remediation and compensation request

Marcus —

Thanks for taking my call this morning. To summarize, FinTechCo experienced two service degradations yesterday (11:03–11:27 PDT and 18:50–19:05 PDT) that materially impacted our payment confirmation flows. Error rates spiked to ~8% and p95 latency climbed from ~180ms to ~1.2s during the windows. This caused a visible drop in completed checkout sessions and triggered notices to our ops team.

We need a formal remediation plan and a proposal for contractual credits or refunds to make FinTechCo whole for the customer/ops impact. Please include: a timeline of root cause analysis, immediate mitigation steps you will commit to (and by when), and a financial remedy framework (calculation method and proposed amount).

Attached is a CSV that maps our business impact to the time slices we observed. We expect executive visibility; I have looped in Anika from our procurement/legal team.

Kevin

[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 9KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Hayes <kevin.hayes@fintechco.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintechco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15 10:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major throughput & latency surge — urgent remediation and compensation request

Kevin — thank you and I’m very sorry for the disruption. I appreciate the timeline you shared — that was very helpful.

Immediate actions:
- I have opened a high-priority incident with infra + runtime engineering. They are already triaging logs and will provide a preliminary RCA within 48 hours.
- We are activating our emergency autoscale policy for your Dedicated pool to mitigate throughput bottlenecks while we investigate.
- I’ve asked ops to produce an SLO impact summary that maps error/latency to SLO breaches. Expect that within 24 hours.

Compensation approach (initial proposal):
- Apologize proactively: we propose a service credit equal to 50% of daily committed spend for each full day where the SLO is breached beyond agreed thresholds, prorated to the impacted time windows.
- We want to be fair and correlated to measurable impact — we’ll provide the SLO measurement and the math.

Can we schedule a 30-min executive readout today at 4pm PDT? I’ll join with Laura (Customer Success) and Rishi (Sales) — they’ll cover remediation and commercial details.

Again, sorry — we take this seriously. I’ll follow up with the incident attachments and the SLO summary.

— Marcus

[Attachment referenced: sso links and internal incident ids]

Team —

Quick prep notes for the 4pm readout:
- Rishi: bring commercial legacy (committed spend, contract SLO wording, renewal timeline).
- Marissa (ops/legal): review typical credit math and confirm internal approval path for an exception if needed.
- I’ll bring the incident timeline and mitigation steps.

High-level asks for the readout:
1) Confirm final compensation calculation and approval authority (does Marissa need GC sign-off?).
2) Commit to concrete mitigation items and timelines we can put in an interim remediation addendum.
3) Agree on communication lines and a shared postmortem delivery date.

Laura

[Attachment: proposed-remedy-term-sheet.docx]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15 13:58 -07:00
Subject: Re: prep notes — commercial framing and quick ask

Couple of commercial points before the readout:
- Contract baseline: FinTechCo has a committed monthly spend of $120k with a 99.9% p95 latency SLO for payment-confirmation endpoints in the contract (see §3.2).
- Proposed credit math: we can do either (A) time-proportional credit tied to the percent SLO breach (recommended), or (B) flat-day credit increments. Time-proportional will be less contentious and defensible.
- We should be prepared to offer a one-time goodwill credit in addition to calculated SLO credits to preserve the relationship — propose $25k as a starting point if legal signs off.

Legal note for Marissa: if we go beyond the standard credit formula in the contract, we’ll need a short remediation addendum executed by both sides. Who has sign-off?

Rishi

From: Kevin Hayes <kevin.hayes@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Legal <contracts@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-04-15 16:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major throughput & latency surge — urgent remediation and compensation request

Marcus/Laura —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and proposed times. 4pm works for our executive team; we’ll have our Head of Ops and contracts lead on the call. A few clarifications ahead of the readout:
- We appreciate a time-proportional approach. Please be explicit in the readout about the measurement window, aggregation method (p95 vs p99), and whether retries are included.
- FinTechCo expects a remediation addendum that includes: immediate mitigation commitments, a rollback strategy, and a schedule for kernel/runtime changes if these are part of the fix.
- Regarding goodwill: $25k is a reasonable starting point; we may ask for more if the postmortem shows systemic negligence.

We’ll join at 4pm.

Kevin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Hayes <kevin.hayes@fintechco.com>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Legal <contracts@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-04-18 16:42 -07:00
Subject: Outcome: agreed interim remedy and next steps (summary)

Kevin / Anika —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Per our discussion, here’s the agreed interim remedy and next steps (this email serves as a working record until addendum is signed):

Agreed interim remedy:
- Measurement: Redwood and FinTechCo agree to use p95 latency for the payment-confirmation endpoint, excluding client-side retries, measured at the ingress gateway. Measurement window: 15-minute buckets.
- Compensation: Time-proportional credit equal to (committed daily spend) * (percent by which p95 exceeded the contracted threshold) for impacted windows. Example calculations will be attached in the addendum.
- Goodwill: Redwood will issue a one-time credit of $25,000 to FinTechCo, applied to the next invoice.

Operational commitments:
- Immediate: Emergency autoscaling will remain active for 72 hours; we will also enable a temporary KV-cache override for your payment flow to reduce tail latency.
- RCA: Engineering to deliver a preliminary RCA within 48 hours and a full postmortem within 10 business days.
- Remediation addendum: Draft to be shared by Redwood Legal (Marissa) within 3 business days for countersignature.

Attachments included: incident SLO impact summary and the initial draft of the remedy term sheet.

If this aligns with your expectations, please reply with a one-line acknowledgement and we will proceed to circulate the formal addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: slo-impact-summary-Apr2026.pdf, proposed-remedy-term-sheet.docx]
